issues.title: Guests cannot use Join: the button spins indefinitely
issues.screens: Circles, Discover circle cards, Circle detail
issues.evidence: Rendered at 320 and 390 pixels; also reproduced in tablet/desktop public views. Join is disabled and busy before any action. For a guest, both pendingJoinScope and circleScope are null, so their equality incorrectly reports an active request. Circle detail repeats the same comparison.
issues.fix: Require a non-null pending scope before treating the operation as busy. Keep the guest Join action available so it can open sign-in. Check the related chat pending comparison without relaxing account-scoping safeguards.
issues.accept: As a signed-out visitor, Join has a readable label, no spinner, and opens sign-in. As a signed-in member, only a real in-flight operation disables it. Test account changes and late responses.

issues.title: Selected tabs and filters are visual only in the web preview
issues.screens: Bottom navigation, feed filters, Discover categories, circle sections; other accessibilityState consumers need the same compatibility check
issues.evidence: On Home, the selected Home tab and For you filter have no aria-selected, aria-pressed or aria-current attribute. The accessibility tree does not expose a selected item. Source supplies accessibilityState, but the installed react-native-web mapping reads separate ARIA/accessibility props instead of that object.
issues.fix: Add a cross-platform control contract that actually exposes selected/pressed/current state on web while retaining native semantics. Use tab selection for real tabs and pressed state for toggle buttons. Audit busy/checked state through the same adapter.
issues.accept: DOM and accessibility-tree checks identify exactly one current navigation tab and the selected filter. Verify changes after keyboard activation; check VoiceOver/TalkBack separately.

issues.title: Most visual screen titles are not semantic headings
issues.screens: Home, Discover, Circles, circle/profile detail, Messages, Create, onboarding and most guest gates
issues.evidence: The 390-pixel DOM captures contain zero headings on these screens despite prominent visual titles. Account Email and the OAuth error screen provide working counterexamples with heading roles.
issues.fix: Introduce a shared screen-title component with native header semantics and web heading levels. Give major sections a logical hierarchy, without making the wordmark another page heading.
issues.accept: Each screen has a useful primary heading and logical section headings. Screen-reader heading navigation reaches the screen title, main content sections and dialog title.

issues.title: Browser pages have no human-readable document title
issues.screens: Web preview: Home and public profile directly checked; route metadata needs app-wide coverage
issues.evidence: document.title is an empty string on Home and /person/2. Browser tab labels fall back to localhost URLs. Existing tab navigation options do not provide meaningful document titles for these rendered pages.
issues.fix: Set page titles such as Home · Circles, Discover · Circles and Jules Park · Circles through the supported Expo Router head/metadata path. Include useful titles for loading, error and private screens.
issues.accept: Titles change correctly on direct links and client navigation and remain meaningful in browser history and assistive technology.

issues.title: Dialogs lack an accessible name
issues.screens: Comment sheet directly inspected; sign-in dialog also needs an explicit title association
issues.evidence: The rendered comments modal has role=dialog and aria-modal=true, but neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby. Its visible title The conversation is plain text. Its close control is announced simply as close. Sign-in has a visible heading but the outer Modal has no explicit title association.
issues.fix: Name each dialog from its visible title and give close controls contextual names such as Close comments. Preserve the observed focus containment and keyboard focus indicator.
issues.accept: The accessibility tree announces Comments or Sign in as the dialog name. Keyboard focus enters, stays within the dialog and returns sensibly when dismissed. Recheck on both native platforms.

issues.title: The desktop search advertises an unimplemented shortcut
issues.evidence: The search button displays ⌘ K. No app keydown/shortcut listener was found in app, components, lib or hooks. This audit did not claim a browser-level shortcut test.
issues.fix: Implement and test the advertised shortcut with the platform-appropriate label, or remove the badge. Keep click/tap search working.
issues.accept: The displayed shortcut opens and focuses Discover search on the relevant platform, and does not conflict with editable fields.

issues.title: Single-item counts use plural copy
issues.screens: Circle cards, Circle detail, public profile statistics/end-of-list
issues.evidence: Existing records render 1 members, 1 moments and All 1 moments loaded. The desktop recommendation row already uses a singular/plural distinction, so the same data is described inconsistently.
issues.fix: Use shared count formatting for member/members and moment/moments, including zero, one and larger counts. Use the same helper in visible and accessible labels.
issues.accept: Counts of 0, 1 and 2 read naturally across cards, profiles, detail pages and accessible labels.

issues.title: Bring actual communities higher on small phones
issues.screens: Circles browsing; Home header can receive the same density review
issues.evidence: At 320 × 740, the circle banner, search, category rail and directory tabs leave only a small sliver of the first circle image above the bottom bar. This is content prioritisation, not document overflow or a navigation overlap defect.
issues.fix: Reduce the banner height on narrow phones or make it dismissible after the first visit. Retain the identity and editorial copy while giving the directory and its first community more room.
issues.accept: The initial phone view shows enough of a real circle card to communicate what can be browsed, while search and navigation remain easy to use.

issues.title: Use consistent names for communities and content
issues.screens: Desktop navigation, Circles directory, Discover, composer, profiles
issues.evidence: Desktop says My circles for a route that defaults to discovery; mobile says Circles. Content is called Posts in Discover/composer and Moments in profiles and feed copy.
issues.fix: Use Circles for the general directory and Your circles for the membership view. Choose one primary content noun, or deliberately explain the relationship between a post and a moment.
issues.accept: Navigation and screen labels match the destination at phone and desktop sizes; users do not need to learn two names for the same object.

issues.title: Replace engineering language in the live lobby with user guidance
issues.evidence: Visible product copy discusses Native WebRTC, a development or release build and a TURN relay. These are implementation details rather than a practical next action for a person trying to join a live conversation.
issues.fix: Keep camera/microphone expectations clear, detect unsupported environments where possible and show a plain-language next step. Move build and relay requirements to operator/developer documentation.
issues.accept: A nontechnical person can understand whether live is supported and what to do next without knowing WebRTC or TURN.
